newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE bases strategy on outcry, eyes new systems.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE bases strategy on outcry, eyes new systems.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Wednesday it remained committed to pit trading but it would renew its electronic systems in an attempt to cut member costs.

After a strategy review held on Tuesday, the exchange said in a statement it maintained its belief that open outcry was the most efficient way to do business, and will remain the main platform for the forseeable future.

But it also said members could develop electronic "hand-held trader cards" and that it would build a new generation electronic trading platorm to replace its APT and APT plus systems for afterhours trade. The exchange also confirmed it was maintaining the option of developing a new trading floor at the Spitalfields site at the edge of London's financial district and to fit out the trading floor at the Stock Exchange by May 1998.
"We understand the pressure on members' costs and must increase the efficiency of our world renowned open outcry trading system," LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth said in the statement.

"We must also respond to the market demand for screen based trading, particularly outside normal trading hours. The decisions made by the Board will enable it to stay ahead in the race for the euro contracts and to develop its business in the years ahead."

LIFFE said its board agreed to embark on an extensive renewal of electronic member support systems such as price reporting, post trade processing, position management, clearing and membership administration.

"LIFFE will provide the basic infrastructure and as much additional support as possible to allow member firms and third party suppliers to develop new order management systems and electroninc hand held trader cards in a way which is compatible with LIFFE's own system," it said.

"It regards this as a more flexible way forward and a more efficient use of resources than developing such systems itself and imposing single Exchange-wide systems on all members." LIFFE said the board felt the time had come for a new generation electronic trading platform.
"The board concluded that there was demand, particularly from the world's major financial institutions, for screen based systems, particularly for after hours."
The exchange said such a system would seek to replicate the sophistication of a trading floor in options, spreads and other complex trades.

"It would build on the pathfinding APT and APT plus systems and the system for automating equity options, currently under development," the statement said. "The board would expect the new electronic platform to be available within the next two years."
LIFFE also said a review of the exchange's governance arrangements would be undertaken and that the board had reviewed the exchange's finances over a 10-year period.
